chapter: Teaching, the 1951 Big Show and New York nights
title: New York versus Los Angeles; Panama Francis and Illinois Jacquet
summary: Collins says New York musicians play from sheer desire, whereas Los Angeles is studio-oriented; he saw Panama Francis with Jacquet's band.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: That's a difference in New York and Hollywood or Los Angeles. Here everybody is studio oriented, you know. If you're in a studio and you make a lot of money, you know,

you're it. New York, they play for the sheer desire, desperation playing, I guess, you know. Just a sheer desire of playing. This is -- you know, this is just New York. You got here-- I go there occasionally now, and it's like a shot of adrenalin. I get around and I hear this vigorous music. It's --
Not just musicians. (Inaudible). The musicians care but they've got --
Yes, yes. But out here you can get lethargic, you know, you can get --

That's right. But in New York, no. It's always something happening, and that I miss. And I hope one day to really I think that I may go back one day. Just -- but I go back once a year now just to listen and to see everybody and I saw Panama Francis there. You know, he was out here for a while, and he was doing very well but he just never got New York out of his system, so he finally said I've just got to go back, and he went back, and I saw him, he

had a big grin on his face, he was playing with Illinois Jacket. Jacques And this band, Illinois' band, was Hank Jones, Percy Heath, Panama, and Tiny Grimes. And it was just -- the band was popping, and Jacket when he saw me it was just beautiful. He ran over and hugged me and played his bassoon, I believe. This was his new instrument, he plays it very well.
